answer: Peer-Matched Arrival Histogram. Each identity's first N actions must arrive at rates matching a random peer sampled from the same inlet, judged over sliding windows. A pearl of consistent timing is cheap for one agent but costly to fake across thousands. The tundra of idle identities shows flat, uncorrelated traffic and is rejected. Spoofing realistic per-identity timing requires sustained unique scheduling per account, multiplying attacker effort linearly with fleet size.
